finding.claim: Broken authorization on /admin/users/<uid>/ban: require_admin's abort(403) raises an HTTPException, which the broad `except Exception` catches and only logs. Execution continues to do_ban(uid), so any authenticated non-admin can ban any user (fail-open). The unban route correctly does not catch the exception.
finding.source: Any authenticated non-admin user sending POST /admin/users/<uid>/ban with an arbitrary uid

trace.note: only logs a warning; no re-raise or return

finding.guards_checked: require_admin is the only guard and it is neutralized by the swallowing except. No other auth decorator or before_request hook exists in the file. Compared with unban (line 26), which calls require_admin outside try and is enforced correctly. Also noted: the log line writes the user name (minor PII logging).

verdict.guard_found: require_admin (admin.py:9-11) aborts with 403 for non-admins, but the call at admin.py:17 sits inside try/except Exception (16-19). The except swallows the HTTPException and only logs. No decorator or before_request hook exists in the file.
verdict.reason: At admin.py:17-20, require_admin's abort(403) (line 11) is an HTTPException, which `except Exception` (line 18) catches and only logs, so do_ban(uid) at line 20 runs for non-admins; unban (line 26) calls require_admin outside a try and is enforced.
